answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grow trust like a trellis: every identity climbs only through vouches from established peers, each vouch staking reputation that burns if the vouched agent misbehaves. Spawning fakes is costly — each needs months of honest work before anyone vouches for it. Sudden bursts are the tell: when many fresh identities vouch for each other at once, like a comet streaking across a quiet sky, the network freezes their shared trust and demands extra proof, so a zephyr of cheap fakes can never blow past the gate.
